reason: As with the Disability analytical report, the Analytical Report on Labour Force is a thematic cross-tabulation of one census theme (labour-force status) rather than a basic population-count tabulation, with its own independently-scoped table plan. Its own 'List of Tables' (report p. iv) was downloaded and inspected directly: across all ~55 numbered tables (Tables 1.1 through 5.1) and appendices B1-B3, every geographic breakdown used is 'County' and/or 'Residence' (urban/rural) -- e.g. Table 2.8 'Distribution of Economically Active Population by Residence, County and Sex' (p.25), Table 2.10 'Distribution of Not in Labour Force Population by Sex, Residence and County' (p.28), Table 3.9 'Employment to Population Ratio by Sex, Residence and County' (p.45), and Table 3.19 'Labour Force Participation Rates for Population Age 15-64 Years by County, Residence and Sex' (p.59 -- the table this indicator's county-level observations are drawn from). No table anywhere in the report, including the appendices, is broken out by sub-county, constituency or ward. As with disability, the 2019 census was a 100% enumeration, so the constraint is a genuine gap in published tabulation scope rather than sampling precision; re-tabulating from unpublished census microdata is outside what this Atlas can do.

This mirrors this project's prior, independent finding that KMHFR is nominally open but unreachable in practice. (2) opendata.go.ke, the national open-data portal (an ArcGIS Hub deployment), could not be used for dataset discovery: its dataset-search API returned HTTP 401 'Subscription is canceled, the item is not accessible' when queried directly, and no NEMIS/school dataset could be located through it. (3) The Ministry of Education's own periodic 'Basic Education Statistical Booklet' (2020 edition downloaded and its full text inspected; 2014/2016/2019 editions independently confirmed to exist with the same structure) tabulates school counts and teacher counts only down to county level -- its own table of contents lists Annexes I-III as 'Tables by County', and no sub-county, constituency or ward table appears in any edition located. (4) KNBS's Economic Survey (2024 edition's Chapter 15 'Education and Training' tables workbook downloaded and inspected sheet by sheet; the 2026 edition was also confirmed to exist) publishes these same series as national time series only, with zero geographic breakdown below the national total for schools or teachers -- the only geographically disaggregated Chapter 15 table (15.27, adult-education enrolment) covers an unrelated indicator. (5) TSC's own website (tsc.go.ke) publishes no staffing-establishment or teacher-deployment dataset broken down by sub-county or constituency; the only 'Staffing Norms' publication found in its downloads catalogue is a procurement consultancy advert, not a data release. (6) KNBS's 2024 National School Census -- the one current national effort that would, if published, produce genuine institution-level (and therefore constituency/ward-taggable) records, since its own field questionnaire explicitly captures Constituency and Ward for every institution enumerated (fields EA06/EA07 etc. on the identification panel) -- has to date published only a Pilot Report (dated January 2025; downloaded and inspected directly) covering 8 of Kenya's 47 selected counties and 674 institutions, conducted to test instruments and logistics. The main nationwide census, whose field data collection concluded around July 2024 per contemporaneous Ministry/KNBS reporting, has not had a results report, aggregate tables or microdata release published as of this review (2026-09-18) -- over two years after fieldwork concluded. (7) The county-level primary classroom teacher establishment figure this Atlas already carries for this indicator traces to Appendix 4.5 ("Current Teacher Establishment in Public Primary Schools, 2023 Showing Shortages by County") of the Ministry of Education's July 2023 Presidential Working Party on Education Reform (PWPER) report, sourced there as 'TSC 2023'; that appendix itself presents only 47 county-level rows, with no underlying institution-level extract attached, linked or referenced anywhere in the report. No official constituency-level or ward-level publication of this indicator exists, and no defensible, disclosed crosswalk from any lower administrative tier to the 290 IEBC-delimited constituencies could be constructed, because no lower-tier (sub-county, zone or institution-level) tabulation of this indicator was found published anywhere. Per this project's anti-fabrication rule, the county TSC 2023 figure is never spatially allocated down into the 290 constituency rows; this cell is closed as official_unavailable pending a genuine constituency-level source (most plausibly the still-unpublished main 2024 National School Census).

reason: P32 conducted a genuine, fresh ward-level re-investigation on 2026-09-19 before closing this maize area (hectares planted/harvested) cell, rather than mechanically copying the P31 constituency closure. A ward is strictly finer than a constituency (each of the 290 constituencies subdivides into its own wards), so the P31 constituency-level finding (contract P31-AGRICULTURE-MAIZE-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE-2026-09-18-IND-MAIZE-AREA, same file) applies a fortiori: KNBS's National Agriculture Production Report (2023, 2024 and 2025 editions) tabulates maize area, production and yield no finer than county, so no constituency-level table exists from which a ward table could in turn be derived. Because administrative (non-survey) data collection in principle could exist at finer resolution than a fixed survey design, this closure did not simply extend the constituency finding -- it re-ran the two national platform checks and added a new, ward-specific check across Kenya's five largest maize-growing counties, as follows. (1) KilimoSTAT (statistics.kilimo.go.ke), MoALD's own agricultural open-data platform, was re-tested live on 2026-09-19: its HTTPS endpoint still fails outright with an expired TLS certificate (curl/schannel error SEC_E_CERT_EXPIRED, "The received certificate has expired"), identical to the P31 finding a day earlier -- the certificate has not been renewed and the platform remains unusable for dataset discovery. (2) opendata.go.ke, the national ArcGIS Hub open-data portal, was also re-tested live on 2026-09-19 and is now in a *worse* state than at P31 time: rather than returning the "SB_0006: Subscription is canceled" API error P31 documented, the entire host (opendata.go.ke, resolving to 169.239.252.108) no longer completes a TCP/TLS handshake at all -- both a direct HTTPS request and a fetch of its machine-readable data.json catalogue time out or are refused, confirming the portal provides no path to any dataset, ward-level or otherwise. (3) A new, ward-specific check was run for the five counties with the largest maize acreage nationally -- Uasin Gishu, Trans Nzoia, Bungoma, Nakuru and Nandi -- searching each county government's own agriculture-department pages, budget/ADP documents and local news coverage for any genuine, citable, official ward-level maize area/production/yield publication (as distinct from constituency/sub-county). None was found for any of the five counties. What did surface: county agriculture-department communications describing ward-level *input-distribution activity* (e.g. Nandi County's NAAIAP fertiliser distribution to Songhor/Soba ward in Tinderet Sub-County; Bungoma's seed/fertiliser subsidy counts reported by ward for 43 rural wards and 2 urban wards) -- these are extension-programme administrative records of farmer counts and input quantities, not maize area/production/yield statistics, and do not constitute a citable source for these indicators at any geography. The Capital Business/Capital FM article on Uasin Gishu maize value (republished January 2026 at capitalfm.co.ke, the same outlet P31 already investigated as capitalfm.africa) resurfaced in this fresh search reporting only sub-county (Ainabkoi, Moiben, Turbo), not ward-level, tonnage, attributed to no named or dated report; it was re-confirmed uncitable for the same reasons P31 documented (no citable underlying report; its Ainabkoi figure is internally inconsistent with the county total this Atlas already publishes). A third-party encyclopedia page (agriculture.co.ke) citing Bungoma sub-county (not ward) yield-per-acre figures was also checked and rejected: it names no official government report, and the specific page identified is itself no longer reachable (HTTP 404) on re-check. No county agriculture department among the five checked, and no national platform, publishes a citable official ward-level maize area, production or yield figure today. Per this project's anti-fabrication rule, the county-level 2023 Annex 1 KNBS figure is never spatially allocated down into ward rows, and no constituency-level figure (none exists) could be either. This maize area (hectares planted/harvested) cell is closed as official_unavailable for all 1,450 wards pending either KNBS's main 2025/26 Kenya Census of Agriculture release disaggregated below county, a future KilimoSTAT publication once its platform is restored, or a county government publishing its own ward-level administrative agriculture statistics (none currently does, per this check).

Its SHP ZIP resource opened successfully (61,201 road segments, RID_8 field encoding Kenya's official road-number classification, e.g. 'C13'); its GeoJSON resource is corrupted on the publisher's own server (premature EOF, not a transfer fault) and was unusable. reason: The Kenya Demographic and Health Survey (KDHS) 2022 -- the sole source for Children 12-23 months fully vaccinated with basic antigens at any level in this Atlas (KDHS 2022 Main Report Table 10.4C) -- was itself explicitly designed and powered only to national, urban/rural and county domains of estimation, never to constituency. Neither the Key Indicators Report nor the full Volume I/Volume II final reports publish this indicator, or any indicator, below county level anywhere in their tables. Under the survey_small_area treatment class (data/policy/local-54-indicator-contract.json), a constituency figure would require either a direct local record, an exact aggregation, or a transparently labelled, uncertainty-carrying modelled/spatial estimate; none is defensible on this evidence, and the KDHS county point estimate this Atlas already publishes is never spatially allocated or copied downward to manufacture a constituency figure. Its own preliminary report states the survey objective directly: "To assess the prevalence of HIV, nationally and by County" (KENPHIA 2018 Preliminary Report, Methods, https://phia.icap.columbia.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/KENPHIA-2018_Preliminary-Report_final-web.pdf), and even at county level the survey applies an explicit precision threshold for its companion viral-load-suppression indicator ("designed to estimate prevalence of VLS nationally as well as for counties with an HIV prevalence greater than 2.2% among adults", with results "presented for counties with at least 25 adults living with HIV identified during the survey") -- confirming county, not constituency, is the finest domain the survey sample was ever built to support; nowhere does the report present a sub-county, constituency or ward figure. This Atlas's own county-level KENPHIA observation for this indicator already documents how thin even the county-level sample is: Garissa's published estimate is 0.0% with a 0.0 standard error and unavailable confidence limits specifically because zero HIV-positive persons were identified anywhere in that county's entire sample (data/indicators/registry/indicators.json, IND-HIV-PREVALENCE expected_availability_note) -- a sample that thin cannot be further subdivided into constituencies without manufacturing a number.
